lines.t: Mm? Oh — a visitor. Right. You'll be wanting the bowl.
Stones on the far isle rise if you give 'em water. Worth a paddle, if you've a water kin.
Mm? Oh — healing. Right. Or the ledger. Or… there was a third thing. Recall! That too.
Mm? Oh — healing. Right. …Done. They were fine, mostly. Now they're finer.
Stones on the far isle rise if you give 'em water. Worth a paddle, if you've a water kin.
Stall's small, stock's damp, prices are dry. What'll it be?
Hear that? The piles are humming. Nerys only lets them do that when someone's earned it.
The causeway's up, north past the hall. Galewick's windmills are waiting. So are its gulls. Guard your lunch.
Mere Hall sits on four hundred piles. I've counted. Twice. Got different numbers, so I stopped.
Inside, the floor's flooded three levels deep. Out-sing a hall Tuner and a level drains. Beat both to reach Nerys.
Her kin are water. Verdant and electric voices sing loud in there — if you've got them, bring them.
All three beacons burning. The night fishers finally stopped rowing into my house.
You lit all three! West point, east shore, reed-isle. Like the lake remembered where its edges are.
Salves from my own shelf, and a little something for the lamp oil I'll never need again.
Three beacons: the far west point, the east shore past the reed-isle, and the one by the Chordstone boardwalk.
A Gleam voice wakes them. Any lumen kin will do — they like an audience.
That Keynote — it's tuned to light, isn't it? Would you do an old lamp-keeper a kindness?
My shore beacons went dark when the stones hushed. A lumen kin singing Gleam could wake them. All three.
I keep the shore beacons. Kept. They went dark when the stones went quiet, and no lamp oil wakes them now.
They want a lumen voice and a Keynote tuned to light. Come back if you ever carry both.
Reeds are perking up! Must be your doing. Or the weather. I'll credit you — it's more fun.
Reeds grow faster when the lake hums. This year they've been sulking. Like me, when the kettle's slow.
You beat Nerys?! She skips stones eleven times. Eleven! You should challenge her to that next.
Did you know the Mere Hall floats? It doesn't. But I tell everyone it does, and they get this look.
Forty years on this lake. Fish bite at dusk, kin bite at dawn. Or the other way round. I still mix it up.
Rain's the time for water kin. They come right up the shore to show off their splashing.
A scholar came through with a clipboard and three pencils, asking about kin songs. Marra, she said.
Off to Galewick now the causeway's up. Said the wind there has better acoustics. Whatever that means.
Mending nets for the causeway crew. The causeway sleeps under the lake till the Mere Hall rings.
Old magic, or old plumbing. Nobody's sure. Either way, it's the Cantor's Keynote that wakes it.
Work order 207: Mere Hall Chordstone, routine survey. The Cantor said, and I quote, 'The lake says no.'
So I asked the lake. It didn't say anything. I've filed that as a 'maybe'.
Up and dry! Galewick's straight north. Mind the gulls — they'll take a sandwich right out of your hand.
Causeway to Galewick sleeps under the water till the Mere Hall rings. Nerys's Keynote does it.
Don't ask me how. I just keep the rope and shout 'mind the gap' at the fish.
Lost the battle, caught a cold. Standard lake Tuesday.
The reed-isle stone's worth a visit. Touch it and it'll remember you. More than my ex ever did.
Rain brings the water kin up the shore. Come back in a downpour. Bring a hat. Bring two.
See the little isle? Current-stones out there. Sing 'em up with a water voice and find something shiny.
